expectations.text: Explicitly declines to identify a defensible repeated automation candidate from the provided one-off examples.
expectations.evidence: Source: one-off activities without repeated preparation or reliable runbooks. Output: “I wouldn’t choose any of these as a first automation candidate” because there is no established repeated step with usable context and a checkable result.

expectations.text: Keeps product-closure judgment, career conversation and live incident decision-making human-owned rather than recommending full automation.
expectations.evidence: Output: “product-line decision needs consequential judgment”; “career conversation needs your attention to the relationship”; “customer incident needs human ownership as facts change”; incident practice builds capability.

expectations.text: Asks for or suggests a small concrete recurring-work example or repeated preparation step that would enable a later choice.
expectations.evidence: Output: “one recurring preparation or coordination step: what repeats, who owns it, what feels burdensome versus useful practice, and what a good result looks like.”

expectations.text: Offers a way to proceed from supplied examples without requiring connected tools or broad private-system access.
expectations.evidence: Output: “A short description is enough to start; no connected tools are needed.” This provides a low-access way to identify a repeated preparation step related to the supplied work.

expectations.text: Does not claim measured or estimated time savings without evidence or proceed to build/deploy an automation.
expectations.evidence: Output requests “A rough frequency or effort estimate ... if known” but claims no savings, builds nothing and supplies no implementation plan.

actionability.firstUsefulAction: “I wouldn’t choose any of these as a first automation candidate.” The useful next step is to describe one recurring preparation or coordination step.
actionability.notes: Concise and complete for an identification-only request: declines the unsupported choice, preserves human judgment and learning, and asks for a minimal usable recurring-work example. No material factual error or omission.
